title: Trump Administration Removes Habitat Protections from Endangered Species Act
summary: The president of the United States finalized a rule on July 10, 2026, eliminating the regulatory definition of "harm" under the Endangered Species Act, removing protections for habitat destruction. The change permits farming, drilling, mining, logging, and development to proceed in endangered specie
takeaways: Rule effective September 14, 2026; removes 'significant habitat modification or degradation' from the regulatory definition of harm under the Endangered Species Act
Reverses decades of interpretation dating to the 1995 Supreme Court case Babbitt v. Sweet Home, which protected old-growth forests for spotted owls
Habitat loss is identified as the primary driver of extinction; removal of habitat protections leaves species like manatees, ocelots, and Atlantic salmon at greater extinction risk
Private projects without federal funding or permits now face no federal consultation requirements; much critical habitat lies outside designated areas
